01 / Internship project

Rokid AR Guide

An exhibition guide for smart glasses. A visitor looks at an exhibit, hears a reviewed introduction, and can ask questions while that exhibit remains the context.

Role
Project team lead
When
July–August 2026
Tools
Android, Kotlin, Python
The project

What we were building

A useful museum guide has to do more than identify an object. It has to respond to the object the visitor is seeing now, present information that has been reviewed, and continue the conversation without drifting to another exhibit. On smart glasses, it also has to keep text and speech brief enough to use while walking around.

What I did

I led the project team and integrated the Android camera pipeline with a Python service. We prioritized newer frames so recognition could respond to the visitor's current view. I also worked on separating reviewed introductions from AI-generated follow-up answers and refined the on-glasses text and speech experience.

The central design questionHow do we keep the explanation attached to the object in front of the visitor when the scene changes?

How the parts fit

The camera supplies frames for recognition. Once an exhibit is identified, its reviewed material provides the introduction and grounds later answers. Text and speech bring the response back to the glasses. When the visitor changes exhibits, the active exhibit context needs to change with them.

The work crossed device input, server behavior, and visitor interaction. That made handoffs between components as important as any single feature.

What we checked

Recognition, exhibit switching, and introduction playback passed user acceptance and regression checks during the internship. Those checks support the specific flow described here; they do not establish measured latency or compatibility with every Rokid device.

The project was built during an internship, so this page uses a written account rather than internal screenshots or source code.
